assembly_notes: The root is `main_frame`, the rigid spine: one merged tube cage of a top rail, a lower towel rail, a wing hinge rail and a lower bar on each side, one leg hinge rail per declared leg station, and end cross members, struts and centre posts at both ends, with black end caps. The selected `spine_extra` is built into that same part, so a spine accessory is never a floating solid. Every rotating child is a captured knuckle rather than a coaxial tube: the moving member carries four open C-rings that run on the fixed rail with a 0.8 mm radial fit, and its own structural tube stands off the axis by the ring radius plus stock. That is what replaces the pool's four `ctx.allow_overlap` families - the wing coaxial with its hinge rail, the leg tube inside its plastic hinge block, the mid-span leg through the centre plate, and the caster against its leg - none of which a Design-backed template may declare. `ctx.allow_isolated_part` is used for the hangers and casters, which really are carried by their own pivots on a running clearance. Leg frames, wings and hangers are all authored in a child frame whose origin sits ON the rotation axis with +X along the rail, so `mate_axes` solves every joint origin and `register_interface_mate` records it. The two wings of a tier share one builder and take the side sign through the joint axis. Wing fold stops are bisected per tier against the spine centreline and, for a lower tier, against the upper tier's underside; the leg fold stop is bisected against the hinge height. Nothing in this file copies a source joint limit.

derived.expression: leg hinge station z minus contact_size_m
derived.name: leg_drop_m
derived.rationale: Whatever the floor interface is, the leg reaches only as far as the top of it, so every ground_contact candidate lands the rack at the same height.

derived.expression: lower bar height minus a leg rail gap of (leg knuckle outer + wing knuckle outer + 6 mm); a centreline station drops further, by the leg clearance plus the shoe cradle depth when that accessory is selected
derived.name: leg_station_z_m
derived.rationale: The leg hinge rail hangs below the lower bar so a captured leg knuckle clears the wing knuckle riding that bar. var_leg_support_count L298-L306 drops its mid-span hinge for the same reason at the centreline; here the drop also clears the shoe cradle, which hangs on that same centreline.

derived.expression: largest q with leg_spread * sin q - leg_drop * cos q <= -0.15 * leg_drop
derived.name: leg_fold_rad
derived.rationale: The frame folds until its feet have climbed to within 15% of the hinge height; beyond that it would be level with its own hinge rail.

derived.expression: spine_height_m * 0.963 for tier 0, spine_height_m * 0.744 for tier 1
derived.name: tier_rail_z_m
derived.rationale: var_wing_count L235-L252 maps each tier onto its own spine rail.

derived.expression: wing_reach_m for tier 0, wing_reach_m * 0.60 for tier 1
derived.name: tier_reach_m
derived.rationale: var_wing_count L235-L252 builds the lower tier at 0.60 of the upper one's reach.

derived.expression: wing_reach_m * wing_rise_ratio for tier 0; for tier 1 the lesser of that at 0.60 scale and half the headroom between the two spine rails
derived.name: tier_rise_m
derived.rationale: A lower wing fits under a steep upper wing by lying FLATTER, not only by being smaller: var_wing_count's single 0.60 scale is correct for its own proportions, and at this template's steepest declared incline a uniform 0.60 copy already stands inside the upper wing at rest.

derived.expression: tier 0: 0.22 + (solved maximum - 0.22) * fold_upper_ratio, bisected against the spine centreline stop; tier 1: the solved maximum itself, bisected against the upper wing sampled across its whole range
derived.name: fold_upper_rad
derived.rationale: Opposing wings may never meet over the spine, and a raised lower wing may never reach the upper wing's underside at any pose the upper wing can hold. A lower tier hemmed in under a steep upper wing legitimately resolves to no raise at all; its travel then comes from its own down stop.

derived.expression: per tier: swept down until the wing member (carrier to tip) comes within (2 * tube_radius_m + 8 mm) of any leg frame's rest shape, or - for tier 0 with a lower tier present - within the tier clearance of the lower wing at rest
derived.name: fold_lower_rad
derived.rationale: Each tier gets its own down stop: the lower tier's useful swing is downward, since it hangs under the upper wing. The leg shape is its real hinge-to-foot diagonal plus the top cross tube standing off the hinge axis.

derived.name: telescope_stroke_m
derived.rationale: var_prismatic_extension requires the wing rail to stay engaged at full extension, which is a fraction of the spine's own length.

derived.expression: leg_drop_m * leg_spread_ratio for a splayed frame, the post offset for a post base, taken from whichever leg family is selected
derived.name: tip_station_y_m
derived.rationale: Every leg family publishes exactly two tip stations, so one ground contact builder serves all three.

derived.name: caster_radius_m
derived.rationale: var_caster_wheels L164 mounts the wheel centre at the tip station, so the wheel radius is exactly the height the leg gives up.

derived.expression: contact_size_m for a pad or a skid bar; 2 * contact_size_m + tube_radius_m * 1.6 for a caster, which hangs below the leg on its own fork
derived.name: contact_headroom_m
derived.rationale: The leg gives up exactly the height its floor interface occupies, so all three candidates land the rack on z = 0 without changing the spine.

derived.name: hanger_pitch_m
derived.rationale: Hangers walk the clear run of the top rail inside the end cross members.

derived.name: hanger_drop_m
derived.rationale: The headroom between the top rail and the lower towel rail is the real stop, measured to the bottom of the CLIP carriers rather than to the body: the source's absolute 0.285 would bury the hanger on a short spine, and a drop measured to the body alone puts the clips through the lower rail.

derived.expression: (spine_depth_m - 2 * tube_radius_m - 0.014) * hanger_width_ratio, then shrunk until body half width + clip, swept through the minimum sway, fits the clear span to a wing hinge rail
derived.name: hanger_width_m
derived.rationale: The hanger body AND its clips have to pass between the two wing hinge rails at every sway angle. Clip size follows body width, so the band is solved.

derived.expression: asin((lateral clearance - 3 mm) / hypot(reach, depth)) - atan2(reach, depth), clamped to [0.030, 0.260], where reach = half width + clip and depth = drop + 1.8 * clip
derived.name: hanger_sway_rad
derived.rationale: A hanger's outermost point is not on the centreline, so the swing that reaches a rail is the ARC from that point's rest angle. Over every body point (L, h) the swept offset is L*cos(s) + h*sin(s), worst at the widest L and deepest h. The sock ring is the binding form: its clip arms fan out horizontally from a hub that already hangs most of the drop.

derived.name: accessory_span_m
derived.rationale: Brace rivet station, shoe cradle drop and towel hoop projection all scale with the spine's own half length.

derived.expression: spine half length * (0.40 + 0.40 * normalised accessory_span_ratio), with both ends on the lower bars
derived.name: brace_end_station_m
derived.rationale: The origin (L286-L287) runs each diagonal from the lower bar up to the centreline at the TOP rail - which is exactly where the hangers hang, and it also lands on the wing hinge rails on the way. hanger_type and wing_form are independent slots, so the brace is re-routed as a crossing pair between the two lower bars, the one rail pair nothing rides. This is the local host adaptation the full-combination rule requires instead of a compatibility gate.

derived.expression: the lesser of spine half length * accessory_span_ratio * 0.42 and 35% of the clear height under the lower rail
derived.name: cradle_drop_m
derived.rationale: The shoe cradle hangs on the centreline under the spine and may not reach the floor; a centreline leg station drops below it in turn.

multiplicities.host_capacity_expression: Station spacing derives from wing_reach_m and wing_rise_ratio, so a shallow wing packs the same count over a shorter incline.
multiplicities.name: bar_count
multiplicities.spacing_expression: Bars, cross wires, comb fingers or drop hooks walk the wing's own incline (or its length, for a comb) at evenly normalised stations, exactly the index-general loop var_bar_count L182-L207 states. The first and last bar keep the source's thicker edge stock.

multiplicities.host_capacity_expression: The spine already carries both rail pairs; tier 1's fold stop is solved against tier 0's underside so a raised lower wing cannot reach it.
multiplicities.name: wing_tier_count
multiplicities.spacing_expression: Tier 0 hangs on the wing hinge rails; tier 1 hangs on the lower bars at 0.60 scale, per var_wing_count L235-L252. Each tier is a mirrored pair.

multiplicities.host_capacity_expression: The spine emits one hinge rail and one end strut per station, and a centreline station's hinge drops clear of the lower towel rail.
multiplicities.name: leg_frame_count
multiplicities.spacing_expression: Stations walk the spine depth evenly between -leg_hinge_y and +leg_hinge_y; N = 2 reproduces the origin's front/rear pair and the middle station of N = 3 is var_leg_support_count's mid-span leg.

multiplicities.host_capacity_expression: Pitch derives from spine_length_m and N, and the hanger body width derives from the clear span between the wing hinge rails, so the sway envelope stays inside its own pitch at every declared count.
multiplicities.name: hanger_count
multiplicities.spacing_expression: Hangers are evenly pitched along the clear run of the top rail inside the end cross members. No record in the pool instantiates a hanger, so the station rule is the template's; see the SourceMap deviation note.

Built from the spine's end cross-member construction, extended outboard on both ends. The only accessory that extends the spine's own footprint along its length.
